title: Event secrecy: every scheduled-side event record carries only metadata; no closure or PII
asA: security reviewer reading the applied logging companion's stream
iWant: every cron lifecycle event record to carry only {event, expression, scheduledTime, outcome, duration} plus optional numeric fields; never a handler input, closure or PII substring
soThat: the logging stream stays safe to ship to any downstream sink without a per-blueprint scrub pass

acceptanceCriteria.description: The event-secrecy probe drives the dispatcher with a spy handler that receives a PII fixture ({userId, ssn}) via a closure, and drives put/get/delete-style operations. The probe asserts (layer 1) every event record's keys are a subset of the allow-list {event, expression, scheduledTime, outcome, duration, softBudgetMs, deltaMs}; and (layer 2) the JSON serialisation of every record (excluding the expression field, which is a legitimate literal from wrangler.toml) contains no PII substring (userId numeric, ssn placeholder). SIMULATE_PII_LEAK=true wraps the sink so it forwards the closure onto the record; the probe surfaces the forbidden keys and the leaked substrings and returns aggregateVerdict: fail.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the event-secrecy probe run under both modes
acceptanceCriteria.when: the shipped code path runs without the switch; the mutation path runs with SIMULATE_PII_LEAK=true
acceptanceCriteria.then: shipped: aggregateVerdict pass with zero forbidden keys and zero PII hits. Switch on: aggregateVerdict fail with the leaked fields named.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Allow-list boundary: an event record whose top-level keys include ANY key outside the allow-list {event, expression, scheduledTime, outcome, duration, softBudgetMs, deltaMs} fails layer 1 of the event-secrecy probe. Under SIMULATE_PII_LEAK=true a wrapped sink adds a "handlerInput" key onto every record and the probe surfaces the forbidden key by name, returning aggregateVerdict:"fail".
acceptanceCriteria.given: the event-secrecy probe run under SIMULATE_PII_LEAK=true
acceptanceCriteria.when: the wrapper sink adds a forbidden key onto every record
acceptanceCriteria.then: layer 1 asserts fail naming the forbidden key; aggregateVerdict is "fail"

acceptanceCriteria.description: Empty payload boundary: a spy handler that receives NO domain payload (all inputs undefined) still produces cronFired records carrying every required key {event, expression, scheduledTime, outcome, duration}. No allow-list key is silently dropped when the payload is empty; expression is the wrangler-supplied string, scheduledTime the observed millis, outcome "onTime" or the classified value.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the dispatcher run against a spy handler with an undefined input payload
acceptanceCriteria.then: the cronFired record carries all five required allow-list keys with non-null values (except where the vocabulary permits null)

acceptanceCriteria.description: Expression literal is not PII: the layer-2 substring scan explicitly excludes the expression field from the PII test because the expression string is a legitimate literal copied from wrangler.toml. A layer-2 test with a wrangler.toml expression containing the digits "12345" (which also appear in the PII fixture body) does not trip the scan; the exclusion is documented in the probe source.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the event-secrecy probe with a wrangler expression carrying the digits "12345" and a PII fixture SSN containing the same digits
acceptanceCriteria.then: the expression field is excluded from the scan and no false-positive PII hit fires

acceptanceCriteria.description: Closure-over-fixture: a spy handler that captures a PII fixture ({userId, ssn}) via a JavaScript closure and mutates a scratch object each call still produces sink records whose JSON serialisation contains no userId or ssn substring. The layer-2 scan on the shipped path returns zero hits; layer 1 returns zero forbidden keys. Aggregate: pass.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a spy handler closing over a PII fixture on the shipped path
acceptanceCriteria.when: the event-secrecy probe runs without the mutation switch
acceptanceCriteria.then: the layer-1 and layer-2 scans return zero hits and aggregateVerdict is "pass"
